description:
The one write that decides a ticket's rigor (ADR-0095). `/acs:ship` judges the path from `plan.md` after `create-impl-plan` and records it on `pipeline-state.json`; every later step reads the recorded value.

The case that matters most is the re-judge refusal. Without it a resumed run would judge again, from the same plan but a different session, and a pipeline could end up half at one rigor and half at another — which is exactly the failure mode the mid-flight escalation this replaced was built to manage.

Profile: ticketed = one open task ticket (TKT-1), unclassified.

cases.title: an unclassified ticket reports no path, rather than guessing one
recording a path prints it back with the reason that decided it

argv: one module, two tests, no stored shape

stdout_json_subset.reason: one module, two tests, no stored shape

cases.title: a path the workflow does not declare is refused
a path recorded without a reason is refused — an unexplained path cannot be audited later

expect.stderr_contains: recorded with the reason it was chosen

cases.title: a ticket already on a path is never moved — the refusal is what makes a resumed run read rather than re-judge

stderr_contains: already on the small delivery path
